F2: each goroutine reduces the legacy error to a metric boolean and never logs it, so a failed legacy write is silent; there is also no panic recovery.
F3: lines 45 and 129 call `recordLegacyDuration` on the storage error path, and line 166 calls `recordStorageDuration` for the legacy `DeleteCollection`.
F4: Delete` now returns on any storage error, NotFound included, before the legacy delete goroutine is started, so a legacy-only row is left behind; the old NotFound tolerance is not visible here, only the absence of any `apierrors` check.
F5: line 139 passes the raw `objInfo` to `Legacy.Update` rather than an `updateWrapper` holding the stored result, so legacy re-runs `UpdatedObject` on its own old object and can persist a different result.
F6: the rewritten goroutines call legacy unconditionally with no `DryRun` check anywhere in the package, and playlist legacy `Delete`/`Create` ignore options, so a dry-run still writes to legacy.
